title: Evaluator fence
description: What a dispatched run may not change. Constitution §4. Read by Noetic.Harness.Fence and asserted complete by `harness validate --only evaluator_fence`.

paths.description: Every entry carries a reason. A path whose reason nobody could write is a path somebody added without deciding.

glob.description: Repository-relative. `**` matches any depth; a trailing `/**` covers a directory's contents.

why.description: What an agent editing this would be able to do to the thing that judges it. `minLength` is deliberate and is not a formality: "because" is not a reason, and the whole value of this file is that every entry carries one.

exemptible.description: Whether a *scoring* attempt may be exempted from this path. `Dispatcher.attempt/3` narrows the fence by the files an environment's task named, so that an environment about the harness's own modules can be scored at all; `Fence.unexemptible/1` refuses an exemption naming any entry without this flag. Absent means false. It is not a weakening of the fence for anything that lands: `dispatch/2` cannot be given an exemption, and an exemption is subtracted from what is judged rather than switching the judging off. The paths that say what passing means outside the worktree a solver was given, such as .agents/** and CI configuration, never carry it.

doc: No `minLength` anywhere: the validator implements a documented subset and *reports* the keywords it cannot check rather than passing them, so a constraint it does not implement is a constraint that lies. That `why` is non-empty is asserted by a test instead.
